A mother brought her five year old to me and said, Doctor, his eye has been turning in since he was a baby. We thought he'd grow out of it.
Stay till the end, because there's a deadline most parents never hear about.
Here's what was happening inside his head. Your brain builds one picture from two eyes. When one eye turns, the brain sees double.
So a young brain does something clever, and dangerous. It simply switches that eye off.
But if that goes on, the ignored eye stops developing good vision. It's called lazy eye, or amblyopia.
Wait, could we still save it? Yes. Glasses, patching the good eye, and sometimes surgery. Treatment works best in early childhood, while the brain is still flexible.
So remember, a squint after four months of age is not something to wait out. Get it checked by an eye doctor.
